findings.summary: onScroll now calls C.ChatReadMessages individually per unread message instead of batching them into a single range-based call via onReadStop, causing N server roundtrips per scroll-stop instead of 1
findings.failure_scenario: User scrolls through a chat with 80 unread messages. Old code: 1 batched ChatReadMessages(range) call after scroll-stop. New code: 80 individual ChatReadMessages(orderId, orderId) calls spread across scroll events, multiplying network requests and server load with no compensatory benefit.

findings.summary: timeoutScrollStop class property is dead code — initialized to 0 and cleared in componentWillUnmount but never assigned a timer ID after the scroll-stop debounce was removed from onScroll
findings.failure_scenario: The property wastes a few bytes of instance memory and window.clearTimeout(0) at unmount is a harmless no-op. The deferred-batch mechanism it supported was replaced by the immediate-read approach, leaving this leftover.
